questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Erasmus grant, not too much administration (compared to going outside of Europe) and opportunity to take relevant and challenging courses abroad

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of assistance from the University of Edinburgh, they had a great 'visiting hub'

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The host institution offered many types of accomodation, I was lucky and found my current accomodation on through a facebook group

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Can be quite expensive if you don't find the right places and quite short-term - don't stress if you haven't found any private accomodation a month or two before your exchange begins

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was difficult to figure out what courses were available but easy to register once you're through the first obstacle

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: through a website link they send to you

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: you could come and speak to officers, I advise that, as they can make changes for you quickly, which you otherwise had to wait a few days

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: OK. was not my top priority, but a lot of possibilities

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: figure out if KU has sent you on a undergraduate or postgraduate agreement - they did not know in my case, which meant that all the courses I had looked for at postgraduate level was not available after all. Very dissapointing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: would've likes to attend the postgraduate programmes (which was why I chose this exact exchange programme), but it was, all things consideres, OK.

Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
Please elaborate on the level of courses *
How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: was divided into lecture - seminar (20 ppl) - tutorial (12 ppl), but lasted only 1 hour and not 2

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
war and justice
advanced topics in global security
multilevel modelling in social science

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: definetely war and justice - highest quality, well-structured, and challenging while not requiring certain prior knowledge
